title: Pre-Analysis — Intake Flap Actuator Standard for a Four-Engine Effectivity Extension
abstract: Closed work order examining whether the twin-engine intake flap actuator standard could be extended to the four-engine fleet, which concluded that it could not without a new bracket.

sections.objective: Establish whether the shrouded bearing intake flap actuator standard, released for the twin-engine aircraft in 2018, could be extended to the four-engine fleet by an effectivity change alone. Two operators had asked for it and the commercial case rested on there being no design work. The work order was raised specifically to test that assumption before anything was promised.
sections.findings_summary: The assumption did not hold. The four-engine compartment firewall sits ninety millimetres further inboard, and the actuator mounting bracket that the twin-engine standard reuses does not exist in that position; a new bracket would be needed and with it a qualification. That alone made the effectivity extension a design change rather than a paperwork change. Two further items were found. The parts figure would have to carry a third variant rather than a two-way pre and post split, which the figure structure does not currently support without a second sheet. The travel check task is written with one limits table and would need a four-engine column, which is straightforward but was not in anyone's estimate. The dust ingress condition the standard addresses is genuinely present on the four-engine fleet, so the request itself was sound and only the route was wrong.
sections.next_steps: Tell both operators that the effectivity extension is not available and why. Record the four-engine bracket as an open item for any future work on this installation rather than closing the subject. Do not amend the parts figure or the travel check task, since nothing is being embodied.

tasks.title: Compare the twin-engine and four-engine compartment arrangements
Check what the parts figure can express
Confirm the in-service condition is present on the four-engine fleet

evidence.similarity_note: Reached from the modification to the figure it replaces parts in, then examined for what a third variant would need.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure expresses a two-way pre and post modification split. A four-engine variant would be a third state on the same items and cannot be shown without restructuring the figure onto a second sheet.
expected_findings.resolution: No action. Recorded as a constraint on any future four-engine work on this installation.

evidence.similarity_note: Found by entity linking on the actuator and shroud part numbers that the task calls out.

expected_findings.rationale: The travel check task carries a single limits table. A four-engine effectivity would need its own column, since the flap and duct geometry differ.
expected_findings.resolution: No action taken; recorded against the open four-engine item.

evidence.similarity_note: Found through the applicability of the retrofit bulletin, which explicitly excludes the four-engine aircraft.

expected_findings.rationale: The existing bulletin already states that the four-engine aircraft are not covered because no bracket has been qualified for them. The request was in effect asking for that statement to be reversed without the qualification behind it.
expected_findings.resolution: Quote the bulletin effectivity note to the operators as the formal answer.

type_data.conclusion: Closed. The effectivity extension is rejected; the underlying request is sound and is recorded as an open four-engine item.
